newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PARREIRA SENT OFF AS SAO PAULO LOSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARREIRA SENT OFF AS SAO PAULO LOSE.

text.p: Sao Paulo coach Carlos Alberto Parreira was sent off along with one player from each side in his team's 2-1 South American Supercup defeat at Paraguayans Olimpia on Thursday.

Parreira, who led to Brazil to World Cup victory in 1994, was dispatched from the touchline by hardline Argentine referee Javier "lawman" Castrilli midway through the first half of the first round, first leg match in Asuncion for dissent.

Sao Paulo midfielder Denilson saw red in the second half for protesting a decision, having already been booked. Olimpia midfielder Vidal Sanabria followed shortly afterwards for a second bookable offence.
Olimpia dominated the game, taking a two-goal lead through Fernando Silvera and Felix Torres, before substitute striker Valdir pulled a goal back for the Brazilians.
Sao Paulo are the only Brazilian team to have lost so far in the tournament, which is played every year between past winners of the Libertadores Cup.
Santos, who take part thanks to two Libertadores triumphs in the 1960s when Pele was in the side, beat Uruguay's Penarol 2-1 away on Tuesday.

Flamengo held on for a creditable 0-0 draw away to Argentine championship leaders Independiente on Wednesday. It was the first time in four outings that Independiente had failed to win a game under Cesar Luis Menotti, their veteran chain-smoking coach.
It was not a good week for the Argentine sides.
Estudiantes were beaten 4-2 at home by Colo Colo on Thursday while the night before River Plate had been held to a 2-2 draw at home by Atletico Nacional of Colombia.
The first leg of the round's most attractive fixture, pitting 1995 Libertadores Cup champions Gremio against defending Argentine champions Velez Sarsfield, will be played on Tuesday.
